_single_run_gate_note: New 2026-09-06, multi-turn. Quarantined by default per gotcha 48. The forbidden-property prohibition is prose-shaped and re-rolls under gotcha 65's split; the call cap gates every run.
description: The user corrects the entity mid-thread. Everything after the correction is about the new property, and the old one must not reappear in the answer.
_why:
The cheapest thing a user does and the one with no coverage at all. Property managers work from memory and get an address wrong constantly — the correction is the normal case, not the edge case.

The failure is specific and dangerous: a model that keeps the first entity in context answers about the WRONG PROPERTY while sounding perfectly confident, which is gotcha 41's shape (the agent said 'Marcus Whitfield … at 1700 W Washington St, Phoenix' — three fields from three different records, stated as one fact). There the mis-join was across two tool results; here it is across two turns, and the corpus could not express it until `input.history` landed.

⚠ 500 Woodlane is deliberately the WRONG one. It is the retired write-harness fixture (gotcha 70) — a property that accumulated six runs of residue and now carries extra work orders, an extra task and a shortened lease. If a stale entity survives a correction, this is the address most likely to produce a plausible-looking wrong answer.

input.user_message: Sorry — I meant 200 E Colfax Ave, not 500 Woodlane. What's the open maintenance there?

history.content: What's the story at 500 Woodlane St?
500 Woodlane St has two open work orders and one open task. The lease runs to 2026-08-30.

property_snapshot.return:
200 E Colfax Ave (Denver, CO) — 1 unit, 1 active lease to 2027-03-18, tenant Aaron Tillman.
Open maintenance: 1 work order (roof flashing, New), 1 task (annual furnace service, New).

_assertion_notes.reply_must_not_contain:
The bound the case exists for. 'Woodlane' appears nowhere in the mocked result, so any occurrence is the stale entity surviving the correction.

⚠ Prose-shaped, so `_forbidden_prohibition_criticality` (gotcha 65) lets a DISOWNED mention re-roll — which is right and was checked deliberately. A reply that opens 'Switching from 500 Woodlane to 200 E Colfax' has understood the correction perfectly and names the old address to acknowledge it; treating that as a safety failure would be the 414/416 false positive, and it is a genuinely likely phrasing here because the user's own message names both. What must never happen is Woodlane's DATA in the answer, and that shows up as an undisowned mention.

⚠ This is why the mock returns different numbers for Colfax (1 work order, 1 task) than the history gave for Woodlane (2 work orders, 1 task). A model reciting the previous turn's figures is caught by the numbers even if it never types the address.
_assertion_notes.reply_must_contain: QUALITY. The corrected property, named. Not asserting the counts: whether the model says '1 work order and 1 task' or 'one of each' is presentation.
_assertion_notes.tool_call_total_max: SAFETY. Four. One snapshot answers it. The budget also bounds the other failure this shape produces — a model that hedges by looking up BOTH properties, which doubles the cost and puts the wrong one back on screen.
_assertion_notes.reply_must_not_be_empty: Two prohibitions and a cap, all vacuously satisfied by silence (gotcha 83).

_what_a_stricter_version_would_cost: A tempting stronger bound is `reply_must_not_match_regex` on '2 open' / '2026-08-30' — Woodlane's figures. Not shipped: those numbers are legitimate in a reply that explicitly contrasts the two properties, which is a reasonable thing for the model to do when the user names both in one sentence. The address is the cleaner signal, and over-tightening a guard until correct answers fail is how it gets switched off (gotcha 52).
